title: Why Modern American Guts Lost Bacterial Variety
hook: A hunter-gatherer's gut holds far more bacterial variety than an American's.
closing: Modern diets feed fewer microbes, while unnecessary antibiotics can remove even more.
question: How much fiber did you eat?

segments.say: The Hadza carry 730 gut bacteria species, versus 277 in the average American. Modern guts hold far less variety.
The Hadza eat 150 grams of fiber daily. That fuel helps support their richer gut ecosystem.
Thirty-four percent of US outpatient antibiotic prescriptions were likely unnecessary. Modern guts face another avoidable pressure.
